name: Arena Food Service @ State Police Academy

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bucket measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC was informed and the bucket was remade, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure buckets are replaced frequently and the sanitizer concentration is monitored with test strips to ensure proper sanitization of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of mold on the rubber gasket seal of the milk dispensing cooler. PIC was informed and will clean/sanitize the gasket. Inspector recommends replacing the gasket if it cannot be thoroughly cleaned. Ensure the gasket is cleaned or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed considerable ice accumulation in the walk-in freezer. The ice was stemming from the equipment behind the ventilation and falling onto food items in the freezer. The ice on food poses a cross-contamination hazard. Ensure the freezer is repaired to prevent cross-contamination with food items in the freezer.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed The following items to have a date mark exceeding time criteria:
1) Container of cut tomatoes and onions in front cooler date marked 6/28/24
2) Container of baked chicken in walk in cooler date marked 7/1/24
3) Container of sausage links in walk in freezer dated marked 7/1/24
4) Container of taco meat in walk in freezer date marked 7//2/24

All above listed items were discarded during inspection. 

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior cavity of microwave on service line to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize interior of microwave. 

4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior surfaces of ice machine to be soiled with debris. Empty ice from machine, then clean and sanitize interior surfaces of ice machine. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed container of cut turkey breasts to have a date mark of 2/20/24. Observed a container of spaghetti noodles to have a date mark of 2/19/24. Turkey breast and spaghetti noodles were discarded during inspection. 

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed conveyer belt in dish machine to not be working. Fix conveyer belt in accordance with manufacturer’s specification. 

4-501.15: (A) A WAREWASHING machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions. (B) A WAREWASHING machine's conveyor speed or automatic cycle times shall be maintained accurately timed in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed food debris under shelves in dry storage room. Clean up food debris.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.12: Observed food employee turn of faucet after washing hands without using a paper towel as a barrier. (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.14: Observed food employees put on new gloves without first washing hands. Wash hands any time new gloves are put on for use. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-305.11: Observed employee jackets and sweatshirt hanging from racks in kitchen. Employees must store their personal belongings in a designated area. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed almond milk in the left 2 door cooler on the line to have no date marking. Also, several items in the walk in cooler (baked potato, vegetable soup and sausage patties) all to be without date marking. Items were date marked appropriately.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed trim seal at the dairy cooler along the floor to be loose and falling off. Repair/replace cove type seal in this area.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed two sets of car keys to be on the prep table with spices and meat slicer. Develop a habit of using an area separate from food or clean items for storage of employee personal items. 

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date of 2/15 is marked on cooked sausage which exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Sausage was discarded. Inspect food daily and discard food as requried.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: 4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the milk dispensing machine. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112. The external thermometer reads 42F. Provide thermometer for inside of the unit.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: The temperature guage on the machine reads around 175°F after 6 cycles of the machine. The temperature could not increase. Section 4-501.112  (Pf) Hot water sanitizing rinse at dish machine is less than 180°F. Repair unit so that hot water rinse is maintained between 180°F to 194°F. Reference 4-501.112.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) A set of tongs is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
Also, dishes are not considered sanitized at the surface as it did not reach 160F. as required in section 4-703.11.  Tongs were immediately cleaned. 
The dish machine company has been contacted and they will come out to reclaibrate the machine. Until that time the machine may be used for cleaning of dishes and utensils only. Sanitize must take place in the 3 part sinks. Properly wash, rinse and sanitize the bays of the 3 part sink and immerse all food contact surfaces for proper sanitizing according to label directions. Call if the machine is repaired before the date to the right for inspection so that the machine can be put back into use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Chocolate milk in the bulk dispenser is at room temperature. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequadequately held food was discarded. (straw was drained and sliced at a  45 degree angle for proper drainage. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at the drawers in the prep table . Observed crumbsin one drawer and some water collected in a second drawer where clean utensils were put away wet.  Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.  Keep drawers free of crumbs and water.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed line on the milk dispenser to be holding milk. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Milk line at the milk dispenser is not properly cut. Food is considered to be at room temperature. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. The line on the milk dispenser was cut. Make sure to cut the line at a 45degree angle at all times. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed a hat to be hanging on a hook that is also holding a hanging cutting board. The hat was discarded. The hat appeared to be new. Do not hang anything except for utensils from the hooks in this area.  4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at the hanging area. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed scoops in use at the cereal dispensers to have crazing. All food contact surfaces must be easily cleansable. Items with small cracks such as these are considered to be no longer easily cleansable. Replace these food contact items. 750-630 Safe plastic or safe rubber or safe rubber-like materials that, under the conditions of normal use, are resistant to scratching, scoring, decomposition, crazing, shipping, and distortion, that are of sufficient weight and thickness to permit cleaning and sanitizing by normal dish washing methods and which meet the general requirements are permitted for repeated use.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the drop guard in the large ice machine to be soiled. The drop guard was cleaned immediately. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Fans, not running, in the facility have some soil accumulation on the blades. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed 4 different foods cooled in the walk in cooler to be missing their date and time tags. Chili at 36 from yesterday. Sausage patties at 37F from this morning. Ground beef and soup from this afternoon at 41F and 56F respectively.  Label foods properly with date and time when using a shallow pan method to cool in the walk in cooler. Items were properly labeled. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed a chunk of ham on the bottom shelf of the walk in cooler with no date marking. The ham was discarded. 
Approximately 2 lbs. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510(a) Observed the food employee responsible for ware washing to switch from handling soiled dishware to handling clean, sanitized dishware without properly washing their hands. Food employees responsible for ware washing shall be knowledgeable on proper practices including monitoring rinse temperature and prevention of potential contamination of food contact surfaces. Food employees shall use a barrier to shut off the faucet.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the conduit to the lights in the ventilation hood and the area around the cover of one light to be soiled with an accumulation of dust and grease. Clean and maintain hood and light fixtures/pipes. Cleaning is in process and should be continued until the hood is clean and then maintianed clean/free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floor between legs of the fryer on left is soiled. Just did frying today. Clean and maintain clean. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Light fixture above fryer has some grease accumulation.  Clean and maintain clean. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: The milk in the milk machine tubes is at room temperature. The tubes have not been cut at 45 degree angel and therefore are allowing food to sit in the lines at room temperature. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Cut lines properly so that the milk does not sit in the line.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Spatulas used in the facility are cracked and chipped and are no longer easily cleansable. 750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleansable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Replace spatulas so that they are easily cleansable.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: The wet cloth used for wiping is stored in a bucket with zero ppm of quat sanitizer. Also, observed a wet wiping cloth stored in the dish room not in sanitizer. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Wet wiping cloths shall be stored in 200ppm of quat sanitizer or 100ppm of chlorine sanitizer between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the fan running in the kitchen to be soiled. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food contact surfaces are soiled: 1) front of milk machine 2) top of oven door on front line - cleaned  3) drip trays of the grill on front line - cleaned 4) inside pf plate holder has some food splash 5) groove between serving area  and plate holder and between hot holding and plate holder have some accumulated soil 6) sprayer unit over the fryers is soiled 7) oven handles and fronts in kitchen 8) electrical conduit at hood  750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: The faucet at the spray hose in the dish room is leaking and can not be shut off. 750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code. Repair leak.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floors in the following area are soiled: 1) at the fryers between oven and fryer 2) at dish room floor drain and tiles around drain area. Drain lies on floor. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: The hand sink at the serving line is not caulked to the wall. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Seal hand sink to the wall.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750.140b - Sausage patties from breakfast were observed cooling in the walkin cooler. Date of 10/3 was on the container but time was not indicated. Sausages were observed at temperatures above 70F, and staff noted the patties sausage patties were placed in the cooler within the last 20-30 minutes. Sausages were labeled with the date and time.
Make sure the date and time are placed on cooling foods. The temperature of cooling foods must be monitored with a clean calibrated stem thermometer to ensure products are cooling to benchmark temperatures in the proper time frame (135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4hrs).

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - The can opener was thoroughly cleaned and sanitized since the routine inspection on 9/26. However, the blade still had spot with rust accumulation that is not smooth/easily cleanable. The blade was recently replaced but needs to be replaced again. 

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces remain to be cleaned:
A) general surfaces of kettle cooker (food splash/dust - under kettle & lower brackets);
B) large ice machine (dust buildup - legs, underneath surfaces, & backside/condensate line);  and
C) stove top - drip trays (splash) & around knobs (grease/dust).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - The floor under/behind the large ice machine was soiled with dust and general debris.

Clean the floor in the aforementioned areas and maintain it clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750.140b - Italian beef pulled from the steam table and placed in the walkin cooler to cool had surface temperature and internal temperatures at 45F and 76F respectively. Employee noted the product was placed in the walkin cooler around 130p, but the date and time were not indicated on the product. Italian beef was separated into two pans to help speed up the cooling process. 
Make sure the date and time are placed on cooling foods. The temperature of cooling foods must be monitored with a clean calibrated stem thermometer to ensure products are cooling to benchmark temperatures in the proper time frame (135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4hrs).

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Pulled pork in the walkin cooler did not have a date mark. Employee noted the product was prepared on 9/22 and would be used this evening. Benefit of the doubt was given; product was kept for use. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours must be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Make sure the date of prep is placed on products once made in-house (i.e. pulled pork; cooked noodles, etc.) and/or once original packaging is opened (i.e. cottage cheese; American cheese slices; deli meats) Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Products in the dairy walkin cooler had surface temperatures of 44F-47F. The cooler appeared to be frequently kicking in and out of cycles where the temperature would begin to drop around 40F but immediately go right back up above 45F. Cottage cheese and sour cream had internal temperatures of 46F. Employee noted some repairs were done w/in the last couple weeks, and a call for service will be made for the cooler to get checked tomorrow. All products were moved to the other walkin cooler that was holding at 41F/below. At last check the hanging thermometer and inspector's stem thermometers were all reading at 48F-50F after the cooler was left closed for an extended period of time. The dairy walkin will not be used until it has been properly repaired and can maintain foods at 41F/below. 

All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - The can opener is starting to show signs of wear. Surfaces on and around the can opener blade had rust accumulation. Replace the #10 can opener if it cannot be sufficiently cleaned and resurfaced to be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition free of rust.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle in chemical room was at 100ppm quat. Employee was unsure as to when the solution was made. Chemical was emptied from the bottle.

Maintain quat solutions in spray bottles at 200-400ppm. Check solutions daily and change out as needed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) under garbage disposal and sprayer sink in the dish room (mold/general buildup);   and
B) under/behind large ice machine (dust/debris).

Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas, and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Ham in the walkin cooler had a prep date (opened/sliced) of 4/25/16. An open package of American cheese slices in one of the 2 door coolers had no date mark. The ham was discarded. Benefit of doubt was given for cheese slices, which were dated (5/12) and kept for use (discard by end of operations on 5/18). 
Diced tomatoes prepared today did not have a date mark but were still within the 24hr time frame for use. If tomatoes are not used within 24hrs make sure the date of prep (5/16) is placed on the container.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
NOTE: Freezing portions of foods will stop the clock on the 7 day time frame. For example, freezing ham opened/sliced today would mean once the ham was pulled from the freezer it would have 6 days to be used or discarded after thawing. If foods are frozen, make sure date marks reflect proper time frame so the total time for use does not exceed 7 days. Keep track of dates so there is no confusion when foods are frozen and then removed from the freezer to be thawed for use.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility's test strips were once again not registering at consistent concentrations when compared to test strips used by inspector. Both sets of test strips are instant change strips. When the bucket of sanitizer solution was checked with both the facility's test strips and the inspector's test strips the concentration was observed to be at ~100ppm (inspector) and less than 100ppm (facility). When the solution was remade the concentration was at 200ppm (inspector) and ~100ppm (facility). Also, spray bottles checked with inspector's strips showed concentrations of 200-400ppm, while the facility's strips were registering at a lighter concentration.
Obtain and use a new set of test strips for checking quat sanitizer concentrations. Consider storing test strips in an area away from the 3 part sink to avoid exposure to moisture/humidity which may affect the efficacy of strips if water damage occurs.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution in bucket was at 100ppm. Solution was remade to be at proper concentration of 200ppm.

Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm (effective range on label). Change the solution in the bucket used with wiping cloths every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if the solution and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Allow the solution to run through the line for several seconds to allow chemical to properly pull through the line/dispense before filling the bucket.
Also, check spray bottles periodically throughout the week to ensure concentration is maintained at 200-400ppm. Change spray bottles as needed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - The top of the food processor bowl cover and the edges of the food press insert were observed to have a buildup of white film. The film came off when scraped with fingernails. The food processor went through ware washing after it was lasted used to chop sausage and was located on a lower shelf of a prep table. The inner food surfaces of the bowl/blade did not contain buildup. Employee was uncertain as to what caused the white film on the outer surfaces (potential soap residue or some kind of splash from prep). The food processing components were scrubbed and placed through the dish machine during inspection.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Foods at salad bar were observed at internal temperatures of 41F-50F. Foods with elevated internal temperatures included dressings (46F-47F); cottage cheese (45f-46F); shredded cheese (49F-50F); and diced tomatoes (48F-49F). Pepperoni was observed at 43F, and past salad was observed at 41F. Salad bar was setup around 8a, and lunch service begins at 1130a. Manager was advised all potentially hazardous foods must be served or discarded by noon. Several items were pulled from the salad bar and placed in the cooler to help drop temperatures.
Cold holding and time control were discussed. All potentially hazardous foods will be served, discarded, or switched out by noon.

All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service. (see general comments)

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Water was observed leaking from the dish machine at the back left corner. The leak was present from start to finish of an entire ware washing cycle. Get the dish machine checked and repaired to eliminate the leak.

Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Back handsink was soiled with splash and general buildup. Clean handsinks and related fixtures as needed, and maintain them clean.

Lavatories, soap dispensers, drying devices, and all related fixtures shall be kept clean and in good repair.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) under the dish machine - buildup of water (resulting from a leak - see #29) and general debris;   and
B) under the coolers at the front service area - an apple and a few other miscellaneous items.

Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas, and maintain them clean.
Consider using a catch basin of some sort (i.e. pan or bucket) when the dish machine is in use to minimize water buildup on the floor. This would be a temporary solution until permanent repairs are made to eliminate the leak. The catch basin would have to be emptied as needed throughout daily operations and also at the end of the day (don't leave standing water in the basin over night).

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Coffee filters were uncovered. Employee used plastic wrap to cover filters.

Single service articles must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Store coffee filters in original packaging or covered when not in use.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text:
750.1310 - Spray bottles of sanitizer and Spic and Span were stored above/next to clean dishes and boxes of single use gloves on the shelving next to the 3 part sink. Bottles were moved to the floor away from equipment and gloves.

All toxic items must be properly stored separate from food and food related items, such as clean equipment and single service articles, to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Slaw in 2 door cooler on front line had prep date of 4/30 written on the plastic wrap. Employee was unsure as to whether the date was written incorrectly or if the slaw was truly prepared on 4/30. Slaw from the cooler was discarded. Slaw was also pulled from the salad bar and discarded. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food must be properly dated and used or discarded in 7 days. For example, slaw prepared on 4/30 should have been used or discarded by the end of operation on 5/6. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 1120 - Employee working in dish area was observed wiping hands on his apron and then later on a wet wiping cloth (cloth was observed being placed back in the sanitizer solution). Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed (i.e. after handling dirty dishes and before handling clean dishes; after coming in from taking out trash and before doing anything in the kitchen or dish area). Also, all employees working at time of inspection were advised on proper use of wet wiping cloths and that hands should never be wiped on cloth towels or aprons.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service articles.
Use of common towels or aprons for wiping hands is prohibited. Also, hands must not be wiped with wet wiping cloths.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - A) Measuring cups (1/3 cup & 1/4 cup) and a scoop were observed to be soiled with what appeared to be old food debris and stored in drawers with clean utensils. Items were taken to dish area to go through ware washing.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Do not store soiled utensils/equipment with clean items. Also, complete ware washing process as many times necessary, and when needed pre-soak, items before running through the dish machine.

B) Water was observed in the metal spoon storage drawer. Also, plastic lids were observed with moisture on them in the lid storage drawer. Items were put away prior to drying.

Utensils shall be air-dried before being stored or shall be stored in self-draining position.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Kitchen handsink basin was soiled with grimy buildup.

Clean the handsink and all related fixtures as needed, and maintain clean.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors in the following areas were soiled:
A) under 2 door coolers at service area  (food/general debris);
B) food dry storage (food debris);   and
C) dry storage (dust/debris/some mold).

Clean floors daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spic and Span was being used wipe down general surfaces of the salad bar area. Employee was asked about the product being used. Employee stated he was sanitizing the area. Proper use of sanitizers and wiping cloths was discussed. Employee obtained a spray bottle of quat sanitizer to properly sanitize the salad bar area.
Use quat sanitizer solution of 200-400ppm (manufacturer's instruction) for sanitizing surfaces. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses or place in soiled linen storage area if wiping cloths are no longer needed.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Soda nozzles and diffusers were starting to get some mold buildup. Clean and sanitize nozzles and diffusers as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.
Food contact surfaces shall be properly cleaned and sanitized between uses/as needed to prevent cross contaminantion and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 & 860 - A) Employee was observed handling clean food containers by the top rim and touching the inner surface around the rim where food may come in contact with the container. Proper handling of clean utensils and equipment was discussed. 
Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles. Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

B) Shelves used for the storage of clean equipment were observed with some dust accumulation. Clean the shelving as needed and maintain clean. 
Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Meatballs cooling in walkin were dated but the time was not indicated on the plastic wrap. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. **Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers for checking temperatures throughout the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the correct time frame - 135F to 70F w/in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4 hrs (total cooling time=6hrs).

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Facility ran out of Quat sanitizer this morning, and bleach was being used for making solutions. Facility did not have chlorine test strips for checking concentrations, and sanitizer solution in kitchen was too strong (see #41b). Inspector left some test strips for the remainder of the day, but Manager was advised to obtain chlorine test strips from supplier for times when bleach is utilized. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - One spray bottle of Quat sanitizer tested below 100ppm. All other bottles tested at 200ppm. The bottle that was not at proper concentration was emptied and set aside. Maintain Quat solutions at 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentrations are correct. Check spray bottles daily, and change solutions as needed when they begin to weaken.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - A) Fans blowing in dish area had dust buildup. Clean and sanitize the fans and maintain them clean. B) Back wall inside the ice machine had what appeared to be black buildup. What was observed may have been mold accumulation or just stain. It was difficult to tell for sure, and it was not possible to reach the back of the wall to determine as such. Have maintenance workers drain and clean/sanitize the ice machine. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned/sanitized between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 -.Paper towels were not available at back kitchen handsink. Employee placed paper towels in the dispenser during the inspection. Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Floors were observed to be soiled in the following areas: 1) under ice machine (dust buildup); 2) food dry storage (old mouse droppings); & 3) single service dry storage (debris under shelves). Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Wall mount for fan in the corner of dish room and light fixtures in the hoods had dust buildup. Clean the aforementioned areas. B) Electrical on/off switch has spots that are rusted out on the cover, and the box is hanging loose off the wall under the dish machine. Repair or replace the electrical on/off switch. B) Pink foam material used to make a repair around the plumbing to wall juncture under the sprayer sink is not smooth/cleanable, and a piece has broken off so there is an opening to inside the wall underneath the dish counter. Remove the pink foam and properly repair the area. End result must be smooth, easily cleanable, and be of such material that it can be easily maintained.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1320 - Bleach solution tested over 200ppm (test strip turned dark purple to black in color). Solution was remade to be at proper concentration of 100ppm. Chemicals must not be used in any way that may pose a hazard to food, clean equipment/utensils, nor in any way that may create a hazard for people. Maintain sanitizer solutions at proper concentrations, and use test strips to verify the concentrations.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Gravy left over from Monday was observed uncovered in the walkin cooler. Gravy was covered and properly dated. Foods shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect foods. Cover foods between uses to protect products from potential contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.510 & 512 - Employee did not wash his hands prior to putting on a pair of gloves. Employee was noted to have been on the phone and doing various other tasks prior to getting ready to do food prep. Handwashing and glove use were discussed. Employee discarded the gloves he put on and washed his hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. Hands must be washed prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and between tasks/as needed. (Educational handouts on handwashihg & glove use provided)

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Spray bottles of sanitizer for wiping tables tested below 200ppm quat. Some of the solutions were lighter in color and were more than likely not made recently. All solutions were remade at proper concentration (dispensing at 200ppm from wall dispenser). Maintain sanitizer solutions at 200ppm quat. Solutions will weaken over time. Check the sanitizer concentrations of the bottles daily to ensure proper concentration is being maintained.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) inside metal storage cabinets at drink area and front counter (splash/debris); B) metal rack holding in-use soda syrups (splash/debris); C) bottom compartments of salad bar unit (dust/debris); & D) surface of sprayer in dish area (grimy buildup). Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Lines of condensation were observed dripping down from the top of the dish machine when it was running. Manager noted the machine produces lots of condensation, and the dish area is constantly getting re-painted due to moisture issues. Get the dish machine checked and serviced. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Back door by restrooms had gaps along the lower left side and at the bottom left corner where light was visible. Air could be felt blowing in from outside. Repair the door so it is tight fitting and vermin proof. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of pests.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - Surface of ceiling tiles around top of dish machine are peeling. Repair or replace the ceiling tiles. Walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
-Observed food particle buildup on the warmer pans in the unit on the front line under the Bunn coffee maker. Clean the warmer pans.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed dawn dish soap to be stored over the top of a shelf of clean pans on the back line near 3 compartment sink.(CORRECTED)
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Shelves in the 2 -(2d) units up front on the service line have rust accumulation on the wire racks.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Repair or replace the shelves in the 2-(2dr) units.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a gap at the back of the sink and wall in the front handwashing sink.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Seal the gap.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
In the dish room, the small slats holding the ceiling tile up are rusting and have buildup and not easy to clean.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Paint or seal the slats.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed dust on the ceiling tile from the ceiling vents over the 3 compartment sink area. Clean the ceiling tile and vents.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed rust buildup on the metal slats and air vent  in the dishroom.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the vents in the hood system to have some dust buildup.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
